hypotheses.justification: This follows from hx and the definition of C.Q. Apply QuasiTab.mem_subtrees_of_atOpt, then induct on QuasiTab.build: expanding build_of_node, the newly introduced type-three node has a label in lambdaTwo; other type-three nodes lie in recursively built children. The build_of_leaf case contains only a type-one node. This argument also covers type-three nodes with empty children. Recover hΔ and use the original proof.

Split on Δ.basic. The non-basic case uses the original proof. In the basic case, hS.basicStep Δ hΔ gives C.stepOf Δ = {Y}, hence C.stepOfL Δ = [Y], exactly as established in satDown_build. Then hlen makes next a singleton, hlab supplies its child's label Y, and IH supplies that child's SatDown. Apply the existing satDown_three_basic lemma. The singleton length rules out the empty-child case.

Only the bound hi' needs replacement. After nonBasicStep produces i and hi, hlab i hi says the child at x ++ [i] has a label. By QuasiTab.labelAt, QuasiTab.atOpt_append and hx, this is impossible unless i < next.length: an out-of-range child lookup returns none. Thus obtain hi' without hlen and retain the remaining proof. If stepOfL is empty, nonBasicStep cannot produce its witness under the satisfaction premises.

hypotheses.binder: (hlab : ∀ i, (hi : i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length) → C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) = some ((C.stepOfL Δ)[i]'hi))
hypotheses.justification: Recover hlab from hx and the construction of C.Q. Using QuasiTab.mem_subtrees_of_atOpt and induction on QuasiTab.build, every type-three subtree with label Δ has children (C.stepOfL Δ).map (fun Pi => QuasiTab.build C.lambdaTwo C.stepOfL (Δ :: Hist) Pi) for some Hist. This follows directly from build_of_node; build_of_leaf introduces no type-three nodes. QuasiTab.atOpt_child and QuasiTab.build_label then give the required child labels. Empty step lists cause no problem because there are no indices to check. Use this recovered hlab in the original proof.
